Done — out of practice runs. Final solution.py passes correctness on all 5 shapes (`status: correct`, check.py PASS every run).

Summary: solution.py implements a fused single-launch CUDA top-k kernel (via load_inline): each block bitonic-sorts 128-element chunks warp-locally (float4-vectorized loads when n%4==0, scalar fallback otherwise), keeps a running top-64 per warp via bitonic merge, tree-merges warp lists in shared memory (race-free load→sync→store), writes a 64-entry candidate list per slice, and the last block per row (atomic counter with self-reset) tree-merges slice lists and emits the top-k. Verified correct across all shapes/seeds; benchmark floor on the remote rig is ~27µs per call regardless of design (kernel-only work is a few µs), with peak_fraction ~0.02 (best measured config kept; CUDA-graph and two-kernel variants tested and discarded as slower).
